text: South Korea's Kospi dropped 12.1% in one session, triggering exchange trading halts. The Kosdaq closed 14% lower. Semiconductor heavyweights Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix fell about 12% and 10%. Regional markets declined, oil prices rose, and precious metals advanced during the same trading window.

meta.note: Single-session index collapse combined with exchange circuit breaker activation.

text: The U.S. Development Finance Corporation announced political risk insurance and guarantees for crude carriers and cargo ships operating in the Persian Gulf. The measure supports maritime trade through the Strait of Hormuz, which handles roughly one-fifth of global crude shipments, during active regional conflict conditions.

meta.note: Financial backstop and naval escort references coexist; primary structure logged as insurance guarantee mechanism.

text: A 15% global tariff is scheduled for implementation under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 after the Supreme Court invalidated prior tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act. The temporary measure can last up to 150 days pending congressional approval and trade-related studies.

meta.note: Prior tariff regime invalidated; new authority invoked within the same policy domain.

text: ADP reported 63,000 private jobs added in February after January was revised to 11,000. Education and health services added 58,000 jobs and construction added 19,000, while professional services lost 30,000 and manufacturing lost 5,000. Wage growth for job switchers fell to 6.3%, the lowest differential since ADP began tracking.

meta.note: Net hiring positive but concentrated; sector divergence creates classification tension between compression and drift.

text: The president transmitted Kevin Warsh's nomination to the Senate to succeed Jerome Powell as Federal Reserve chair. A senator stated he would block consideration until a criminal investigation of Powell ends. Powell disclosed an investigation tied to Federal Reserve renovation spending and Senate testimony.

meta.note: Nomination action and institutional obstruction coexist within same governance node.

text: Nvidia stated its $30 billion investment in OpenAI may be its final direct funding before a potential IPO. The prior $100 billion multi-year investment framework was described as unlikely to proceed. The funding round totals $110 billion and includes commitments from Amazon and SoftBank.

meta.note: Prospective IPO referenced but not timestamped; entry constrained to the announced investment boundary.
